overview.headline: DNA stores hereditary instructions in a double helix

keyPoints.point: Students learn that DNA is the hereditary material in humans and other organisms.
keyPoints.quote: DNA, or deoxyribonucleic acid, is the hereditary material in humans and almost all other organisms.

keyPoints.point: Students learn that human DNA includes about 3 billion bases that are the same in all people.
keyPoints.quote: Human DNA consists of about 3 billion bases, and more than 99 percent of those bases are the same in all people.

keyPoints.point: Students learn that DNA bases pair to form units called base pairs.
keyPoints.quote: DNA bases pair up with each other, A with T and C with G, to form units called base pairs.

keyPoints.point: Students learn that an important property of DNA is the ability to replicate into copies.
keyPoints.quote: An important property of DNA is that it can replicate, or make copies of itself.

keyTerms.gloss: Hereditary material present in humans and other organisms
keyTerms.quote: DNA, or deoxyribonucleic acid, is the hereditary material in humans and almost all other organisms.

keyTerms.gloss: Chemical base that pairs with thymine in the code
keyTerms.quote: The information in DNA is stored as a code made up of four chemical bases: adenine (A), guanine (G), cytosine (C), and thymine (T).

keyTerms.gloss: Combined unit of a base, sugar and phosphate
keyTerms.quote: Together, a base, sugar, and phosphate are called a nucleotide.

keyTerms.gloss: Spiral structure formed by two long strands
keyTerms.quote: Nucleotides are arranged in two long strands that form a spiral called a double helix.

keyTerms.gloss: Small amount of DNA found in the mitochondria
keyTerms.quote: but a small amount of DNA can also be found in the mitochondria (where it is called mitochondrial DNA or mtDNA)
